Disruptive Behavior in a Child

oppositional defiant disorder · conduct disorder · intermittent explosive disorder · disruptive mood dysregulation disorder · the antisocial personality age ruleDefiance, violated rights, impulsive rage, or constant irritability between outbursts?

1Script2Urgent3Differential4Workup5Criteria6Severity7Treatment8Follow-upPractice
1Illness script
Bottom line
  • Sort by what the child does then by the mood between episodes
  • Defies adults, no violated rights oppositional defiant; violates others' rights or major rules conduct
  • Outbursts with calm between intermittent explosive; irritable between disruptive mood dysregulation
What it is

A pattern of disruptive behavior in a child, sorted into four disorders

Driver

What the child does (defiance, violated rights, impulsive rage) the mood between episodes

Triggers

Early onset: conduct disorder before 10 carries a poorer prognosis

ADHD (attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder), common alongside, also brings disruptive and impulsive behavior

Chain

Oppositional defiant disorder often comes first conduct disorder antisocial personality disorder at 18, if conduct disorder began before 15

Insights

Irritable or angry mood between outbursts belongs only to disruptive mood dysregulation disorder

A preschooler who cannot make himself understood: tantrums point to a language disorder

3Differential
Disruptive behavior, most tempting first
DisorderFingerprintDecides it
Oppositional defiant disorderArgues, defies, vindictive; deliberately annoys and blames others6 months or more; no stealing or violation of others' rights
Conduct disorderAggression, destruction, theft, truancy; lies for gain or to avoid consequences3 or more in 12 months; violates others' basic rights or major rules
Intermittent explosive disorderImpulsive outbursts out of proportion, not planned; may feel remorse afterAge 6 or older; appropriate behavior between outbursts
Disruptive mood dysregulation disorderSevere outbursts, 3 or more a weekOnset before 10, diagnosed 6 to 18; irritable or angry between outbursts
Antisocial personality disorderPervasive disregard for others' rights18 or older, conduct disorder before 15
Disruptive and impulsiveNo aggression or pattern of violating norms
Reactive attachment disorderAfter abuse or neglect: withdrawn, does not seek or respond to comfort, limited positive affect, unexplained irritability, fear or sadness even in safe settingsSigns before age 5; makes eye contact and plays with varied toys, unlike autism; overfamiliarity with strangers is disinhibited social engagement disorder instead
Tantrums in a preschooler who cannot make himself understoodOther milestones on target; language behind
Behavior only with useThe sole diagnosis when the behavior occurs only with use
4Workup
Clues that change the answer
CluePoints toNext move
Oppositional defiant disorderADHD is more common alongside itAssess for ADHD and treat it if present
Criteria met for both disruptive mood dysregulation and oppositional defiant disorderPrecedenceDiagnose disruptive mood dysregulation disorder only
Behavior only while using a substanceSubstance useThe sole diagnosis
Five-year-old with tantrums; other milestones on targetLanguage disorderCheck language against age
Withdrawn child after neglect who does not respond to comfort; irritable, fearful or sad even in safe settingsReactive attachment disorderConsistent, responsive caregiving; parenting skills and family counseling

Pause point. The bait: conduct disorder for a defiant child who argues and is vindictive but never steals, destroys or violates others' rights. Without those, it is oppositional defiant disorder.

5Diagnostic criteria
Defining rules
DisorderRule
Oppositional defiant disorder4 or more symptoms for 6 months, with someone other than a sibling; under 5 most days, 5 or older at least weekly
Conduct disorder3 or more in 12 months, from aggression, destruction, deceit or theft, serious rule violations
Intermittent explosive disorderVerbal aggression on average twice a week for 3 months, or 3 destructive outbursts in 12 months; age 6 or older
Disruptive mood dysregulation disorderOutbursts 3 or more a week, irritable between, in 2 or more settings, 12 months or more without a 3-month gap
PrecedenceWhen disruptive mood dysregulation disorder is met, do not also diagnose oppositional defiant or intermittent explosive disorder
Time frames
DisorderHow oftenHow long

Conduct disorder3 or more behaviorsWithin 12 months

Practice
  1. 15-year-old boy brought in after a second police warning a year of skipping school, stealing from stores and forging his father's checks set fire to a neighbor's shed last month T 36.8 °C · urine toxicology negative → Conduct disorder → theft, forgery, truancy and fire setting over a year violate others' rights and major rules: conduct disorder; oppositional defiant disorder is less severe and lacks theft and destruction, and antisocial personality disorder needs age 18 or older
  2. 8-year-old girl, 9 months of arguing with her parents and teacher refuses requests, blames her sister, says spiteful things every week no fights, theft, damage, lying, truancy or running away T 36.9 °C · examination normal → Oppositional defiant disorder → argumentative, defiant and vindictive behavior toward adults for at least 6 months, weekly or more: oppositional defiant disorder; conduct disorder is more severe, and she shows none of its categories; there are no severe outbursts with irritability between them
  3. 16-year-old boy, since age 14 erupts over small frustrations broke things in 3 separate outbursts this year; ashamed afterward even-tempered between outbursts; no lying, theft or truancy HR 78/min · urine toxicology negative → Intermittent explosive disorder → impulsive outbursts out of proportion and not premeditated, with calm between them: intermittent explosive disorder; conduct disorder adds deceit, theft or truancy, and disruptive mood dysregulation disorder needs persistent irritability between outbursts and onset before age 10
  4. 10-year-old boy, 14 months of rages at home and at school screams and throws things 4 or 5 times weekly over small limits angry or grumpy most of every day between began at age 8 T 37.0 °C · examination normal → Disruptive mood dysregulation disorder → severe outbursts 3 or more times a week with irritable mood between them for over 12 months, starting before age 10: disruptive mood dysregulation disorder; when its criteria are met, oppositional defiant disorder and intermittent explosive disorder are not diagnosed
  5. 9-year-old boy, a year of fights, theft and truancy attentive in class; no substance use no aggression since a school change; parents ask what helps T 36.8 °C · BP 104/66 mm Hg → Parent management training → conduct disorder is treated mainly with psychosocial care: behavioral parent management training, with cognitive behavioral therapy for older children; multisystemic therapy is for adolescents with more severe symptoms, and risperidone is reserved for severe aggression unresponsive to psychosocial care
  6. 5-year-old boy whose kindergarten teacher reports he shoves classmates who misunderstand him speaks in short, jumbled sentences; cannot count to 10 or name letters buttons his coat, hops on one foot, follows game rules hearing normal · T 36.7 °C → Language disorder → at 5, children speak in full sentences, count to 10 and name letters; aggression from not being understood points to a language disorder when other milestones are on target, and neither disruptive mood dysregulation disorder nor intermittent explosive disorder is diagnosed before age 6
Pairs with School Difficulty in a Child: inattention and learning, not norm-breaking. Developmental Milestones and Normal Growth: is language delayed for age?
Transferable rule

Name the behavior first, then check the age gate: no antisocial personality disorder before 18, and no disruptive mood dysregulation disorder before 6.
